newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela TEMs major factor in cenbank oper losses.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela TEMs major factor in cenbank oper losses.

text.p: Continuing operating losses at Venezuela's Central Bank are in large part due to the financing costs of TEM bills, a bank director was quoted as saying in financial daily Economia Hoy.
Central Bank director Domingo Maza Zavala said, however, that a $3.8 billion government mega-bond will be used to back Central Bank placement of the Treasury bills in open market operations.
The bond "will substantially reduce the Bank's financing costs," Maza Zavala said.

The Bank has an estimated 2.4 trillion bolivars ($4.9 billion) of TEMs currently outstanding, and is expected to increase the amounts issued with wage increases in the public sector, according to analysts.
But legislators say the long-awaited bond issue is stalled.
"We've approved it, I don't know where it is now," Carmelo Lauria, the head of Venezuela's powerful Finance Commission told Reuters Tuesday.

The bank suffered total operating losses of 103 billion bolivars ($214 million) in the second half of 1996, largely on financing the costs of its Monetary Stabilization notes (TEMs), which it uses to soak up excess liquidity.
The article quoted Maza Zavala as saying the losses were not a sign of bankruptcy.
"The Central Bank is a state bank ... it doesn't pursue profits, but sound monetary policy ... Of course, in doing so, it incurs costs," Central Bank director Domingo Maza Zavala said.

National State Deposits Guarantee Fund (Fogade) also has a 1.3 trillion bolivar debt to the Central Bank ($2.7 billion). The Fund recently presented plans to Congress to pay off its debt along similar lines to the government's proposed mega-bond.
